title: Spotify
lede: Import your liked tracks to build an artist → genre dictionary. Then the “My files” module uses it to sort your MP3s.
completeTip: Fills missing genres via Spotify, iTunes, and Deezer. Writes nothing to your local library.
updateTip: Re-downloads your likes list from Spotify to update the dictionary
disconnectTip: Disconnects Spotify (learned base stays on the PC)
needDesktopHint: To link Spotify, open BassOrder as a desktop app (pnpm tauri dev), not browser alone.
sessionKnownTitle: Account already known — revive the connection
sessionKnownBody: The dictionary ({{count}} likes) is kept. Click connect to resume the session — often without Spotify re-login.
step1Title: Your Spotify likes become a dictionary
step1Body: Each Spotify account (Personal, DJ…) has its own connection and dictionary — all stays in your user profile. Search everywhere with Ctrl+K.
stepCreateApp: Create a free app on developer.spotify.com/dashboard
stepRedirect: In the Spotify app, add these Redirect URIs: http://127.0.0.1:41821/callback and http://127.0.0.1:41822/callback
stepUserMgmt: In User Management, add your Spotify account (the one that likes tracks)
stepClientId: Paste the Client ID below, click connect, authorize in the browser — likes import then starts automatically
saveProfileTitle: Saves this Client ID under a name (Personal, DJ…) to find it later
deleteProfileTitle: Removes this profile from BassOrder (not your Spotify account)
connectImport: Connect Spotify and import my likes
connectTitle: Resumes Spotify session (refresh) or opens the browser if needed
avatarOfferBody: It will replace your monogram in the rail and on your BassOrder profile.
apiNote: This is not a bug in your import: since 2025, the Spotify API often returns genres: [] even for big artists. Multi-source completion (related + dict + iTunes / Deezer + MusicBrainz) raises coverage. We sort artists, not each track. Then in My files, Refresh then Guess genres.
noArtistsListed: No artist listed for this folder.
invalidClientIdSave: Paste a valid Spotify Client ID (32 hex chars) before saving.
invalidClientId: Invalid Spotify Client ID (expected: 32 hexadecimal characters).
toastProfileSavedBody: {{name}} · session & dictionary separate from other profiles.
toastInvalidClientIdBody: Paste the ID from the Spotify developer dashboard.
toastConnectingKeep: Resuming session — your existing dictionary will be kept.
toastConnectingAuth: Resuming session if already linked — otherwise authorize BassOrder in the browser.
toastLinkedKeep: Session OK · {{count}} likes already in dictionary. No new import — use “Update” if you want to rescan.
toastFirstImport: First connection — fetching your likes to build the base.
toastDictReadyBody: {{likes}} likes · {{classified}} artists sorted. Go to My files → Refresh analysis to benefit.
toastImportLikesBody: This can take a while — progress shows here.
toastEnrichStartedBody: 3 steps: Spotify, related artists, then iTunes/Deezer. You can leave it running.
toastEnrichDoneBody: {{classified}}/{{artists}} artists with a folder. Then refresh My files analysis.
toastDisconnectedBody: Knowledge base stays on the PC until you rebuild it.
toastAvatarBody: Your Spotify PP is now your avatar.
toastProfileSwitchStored: Session to revive — Connect resumes without starting over.
toastProfileSwitchIdle: Active profile — session separate from other accounts.
feedSyncSubtitle: Building the artist dictionary from your account.
feedSyncHint: Patience — a large account = more pages to load.
feedArtistsSubtitle: We request Spotify sheets. Note: the genres field is often empty since 2025 — not a BassOrder bug.
feedArtistsHint: Let it run — the first progress may take a minute.
feedRelatedSubtitle: Spotify no longer gives genres: we look at related artists and propagate folders already sorted in your dictionary.
feedRelatedHint: Read-only — nothing is changed on your account.
feedCatalogSubtitle: iTunes / Deezer pass for artists still without a folder.
feedCatalogHint: Then MusicBrainz for the priority rest.
feedMbSubtitle: Community MusicBrainz tags — slow (~1 artist/s) but useful when Spotify is empty.
feedMbHint: Priority to most-liked artists still “To sort”.
feedDoneSubtitle: Saving the result on your PC.
feedWaitingSlow: Spotify is responding slowly — the clock is ticking, the queue is running. First visible progress as soon as a sheet comes back.

sync: Opening your liked library, page by page…
Each like feeds the artist dictionary.
No file on your PC is touched for now.
The more likes you have, the longer the first pass — that’s normal.
Next we can fill missing genres automatically.
You can switch screens: import keeps running in the background.
We only read what Spotify exposes to the app — nothing is changed on your account.
Artist duplicates are merged on the fly.
enrich: Read-only: your Spotify account is not modified.
Four steps: Spotify → related+dict → iTunes/Deezer → MusicBrainz.
You can change pages: completion keeps running in the background.
One sorted artist = all their likes sorted at once.
Let it run — thousands of artists take time.
Nothing is written to your Windows folders during this step.
artists: Spotify throttles developer apps: we query artist by artist.
Batch requests often failed — switched to one-by-one, more reliable.
Each sheet brings the official name and, sometimes, raw genres.
Many artists have an empty genre list from the API — we catch up later.
The queue advances even if the percentage stays low at first.
No local write: we only fill the in-memory dictionary.
If Spotify throttles, we slow down automatically — patience.
Already sorted artists are skipped to save time.
Goal of this step: get whatever Spotify is willing to give.
Next we’ll cross with related artists to fill the gaps.
related: When the sheet is empty, we look at related artists to vote a style.
Several neighbors of the same genre = a stronger signal.
Still read-only — Spotify is not modified.
This pass often saves YouTube dumps / mixtapes without tags.
We don’t force it: if the signal is too weak, we move to catalogs.
Spotify links look like a taste map — we use that.
catalog: Last catalog pass: iTunes and Deezer for still-fuzzy artists.
Public catalogs fill what the Spotify API leaves empty.
We ask for the main genre, then map it to a BassOrder folder.
Failures are remembered so we don’t ask the same question in a loop.
Then MusicBrainz for the most-liked still “To sort”.
Network reads only: your MP3s stay where they are.
musicbrainz: MusicBrainz: community tags, ~1 artist / second (server politeness).
We prioritize the artists you like most.
No need to stay on this screen — it keeps going in the background.
After this, refresh My files then “Guess genres”.
done: You can now refresh the My files analysis.
